evidence: No ABX464/obefazimod trial in asthma exists (its clinical program is UC, Crohn's, RA, COVID-19); but miR-124-3p — the exact effector obefazimod upregulates — suppresses allergic airway inflammation, eosinophilia and IL-4/IL-13 in the ovalbumin asthma mouse model (Liu 2023, Immun Inflamm Dis, PMC9896513), and asthma is a Th2 inflammatory disease in obefazimod's anti-inflammatory wheelhouse. The target NCBP1/NCBP2 (nuclear cap-binding complex) is a housekeeping RNA-processing complex, not a druggable class with competing asthma programs, so no target_class precedent applies.

No ABX464 trial in HCM, and the mechanism points the wrong way: miR-124 (which obefazimod UPREGULATES) is INCREASED in failing hearts and its overexpression AGGRAVATES cardiac hypertrophy/dysfunction by suppressing CD151-facilitated angiogenesis (Hua 2018, PMC5865677). HCM is a sarcomeric-contractility disease whose clinical pipeline is myosin inhibitors (mavacamten, aficamten), mechanistically unrelated to the cap-binding complex/miR-124 — the nomination appears to be a spurious genetic-ontology roll-up artifact.

Basimglurant (RG7090/RO4917523), a different mGluR5 negative allosteric modulator, was tested as adjunctive therapy for MDD in a 333-patient Phase IIb randomized trial (JAMA Psychiatry 2016, PMID 27304433); AZD2066, another mGluR5 NAM, was also trialed in MDD. AFQ056 itself was not confirmed in a registered MDD trial (its registry programs were fragile X, L-dopa dyskinesia, Huntington chorea, OCD, smoking), though one secondary source states it 'failed proof of concept studies in depression.'

AFQ056/mavoglurant was directly tested in registered clinical trials for behavioural/psychiatric disorders including obsessive-compulsive disorder (Phase II) and fragile X syndrome behavioural symptoms (Phase IIb/III, e.g. NCT01348087, NCT00718341), placing this drug squarely within the 'mental or behavioural disorder' rollup.

Riluzole, an antagonist of metabotropic glutamate receptor signaling (GRM1), reached a Phase II trial in advanced melanoma (Mehnert 2018, PMC6013351); additionally GRM5/mGluR5 ectopic expression directly induces melanoma in transgenic mice (PNAS 2011, PMID 21896768), and GRM is expressed by >60% of human melanomas, giving strong target-class clinical and preclinical precedent.

The transgenic TRP1-mGluR5 melanoma model produces cutaneous (nodular dermal, hyperpigmented skin) tumors (PNAS 2011, PMID 21896768), and the riluzole Phase II melanoma trial (PMC6013351) enrolled patients with advanced cutaneous melanoma, providing class-level clinical precedent for the GRM5 target in cutaneous melanoma.

mGluR5 is expressed in both retinal plexiform layers and ON-bipolar/photoreceptor pathways, and suppressing mGluR5 over-activation improved retinal function in RCS rats (a retinal degeneration model; PMID 28615682). No clinical trial of AFQ056 or any mGluR5 modulator exists for retinal detachment specifically; evidence is mechanistic/preclinical only.

AZD2014 (vistusertib) has multiple registered oncology trials, including a Phase II in TSC1/2-mutant solid cancers (NCT03166176) and a Phase II in RICTOR-amplified solid cancers (NCT03166904); the entire clinical program is in cancer.

This broad ontology roll-up is anchored by a real clinical program: AZD2014 was tested in a randomised Phase 2 study versus everolimus in patients with VEGF-refractory metastatic clear cell renal (kidney) cancer (PubMed 26364551), a urinary-system malignancy.

A randomised Phase 2 study compared AZD2014 (50 mg BID) versus everolimus in patients with VEGF-refractory metastatic clear cell renal cancer (Powles et al., PubMed 26364551); AZD2014 PFS/OS were inferior to everolimus, but a direct kidney-cancer trial exists.
AZD2014 was directly trialed in renal cell carcinoma: a randomised Phase 2 study of AZD2014 versus everolimus in VEGF-refractory metastatic clear cell renal cell cancer (PubMed 26364551).

No AZD2014 trial in RA was found, but same-target (mTOR) inhibitors are in clinical trials for RA: a randomized open-label low-dose sirolimus trial in active RA (PMC6874993) and an everolimus + methotrexate randomized placebo-controlled RA trial.

AKT1 is an established schizophrenia susceptibility gene (DRD2-AKT1-GSK3beta is the pathway downstream of antipsychotics; Akt1-deficient mouse models show schizophrenia-like deficits, JCI 2008 / PNAS 2007), but no AKT inhibitor is in clinical trials for schizophrenia. Therapeutic direction is inverted: antipsychotics/lithium restore AKT1 signaling, whereas AKT inhibitors like capivasertib (M2698 trial) caused psychiatric adverse events in ~29% of patients, so the genetic link supports the target-disease connection only at the preclinical/mechanistic level.

PI3K/AKT is a central insulin/adipogenesis pathway and Akt3-knockout mice are protected from diet-induced obesity (PMC5752373), but no AKT inhibitor (or any AKT-targeting drug) has reached clinical trials for obesity; reviews note 'no target drug based on Akt has been developed.' Link is preclinical/mechanistic only, with inverted direction (AKT inhibition impairs metabolic insulin signaling).

Human AKT2 loss-of-function mutations cause severe insulin resistance and diabetes (Science 2004, NCT none), establishing a strong genetic target-disease link, but this is evidence AGAINST capivasertib treating it: the AKT inhibitor capivasertib (Truqap) itself causes hyperglycemia in 37% of patients and can trigger diabetic ketoacidosis (FDA label). No AKT-inhibitor trial exists for diabetes; link is genetic/preclinical with inverted therapeutic direction.

Same AKT2 genetics as type 2 diabetes (loss-of-function AKT2 mutation -> insulin resistance and diabetes, Science 2004). No AKT-inhibitor clinical program for diabetes; capivasertib induces hyperglycemia/DKA (FDA Truqap label, ~37% increased fasting glucose), so the genetic association links target to disease at the preclinical level but the inhibitor worsens rather than treats it.

AZD5363/capivasertib (Truqap) is FDA-approved (Nov 16, 2023) with fulvestrant for HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer with PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations (CAPItello-291), and has numerous registered trials across breast cancer, B-cell lymphoma (CAPITAL), TNBC, and AKT-altered solid tumors (NCI-MATCH subprotocol Y, NCT04439123).

AZD8931 was a registered targeted-therapy arm in the SAFIR02_Lung phase II trial (NCT02117167) in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, and was also offered in the SAFIR02L/SAFIRO2L bioguided-therapy lung program.

AZD8931 (sapitinib) is a clinical-stage anticancer pan-ErbB inhibitor with multiple registered oncology trials: gastric/GEJ cancer (NCT01579578, terminated), advanced solid tumours/breast cancer (NCT00900627), and NSCLC (NCT02117167).

No AZD8931 trial in SCC exists (only preclinical activity in SCC cell lines), but the same target class is clinically validated in SCC: cetuximab, an EGFR inhibitor, is FDA-approved for squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck.

indication: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
evidence: AZD8931 in HNSCC is only preclinical (SNU repository study of sapitinib as adjuvant chemotherapy in HNSCC; potent vs gefitinib/lapatinib in HNSCC cell lines), but the EGFR-targeting class drug cetuximab is FDA-approved (2006) for HNSCC, including with radiation and platinum-based chemo.

Synonymous with head and neck cancer; no AZD8931 clinical trial here, but the EGFR inhibitor cetuximab (same target class, EGFR/ERBB) is FDA-approved for recurrent/metastatic and locoregional head and neck cancer.

Azilsartan is in direct clinical trials for renal/urinary indications: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05753696 'Azilsartan in Patients With Diabetic Kidney Disease and Hypertension', and a published randomized crossover RCT (Karger Kidney Blood Press Res 2023, PMID 33677450) showed azilsartan 20 mg reduced proteinuria in CKD patients more potently than candesartan.

Azilsartan medoxomil (Edarbi) was FDA-approved Feb 2011 for treatment of hypertension based on 7 randomized double-blind Phase 3 trials (>5,900 patients), where it was superior to highest approved doses of olmesartan and valsartan; essential hypertension is the on-label indication.
Hypertension is azilsartan medoxomil's (Edarbi) primary FDA-approved on-label indication (2011), supported by multiple Phase 3 trials and used alone or with other antihypertensives.

The J-TASTE randomized controlled trial (Sci Rep 2023, PMC10397297) evaluated azilsartan vs candesartan in HFpEF/HFmrEF heart-failure patients for left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, with fewer new-onset atrial fibrillation events in the azilsartan arm — a registered cardiovascular clinical program for the drug, though not a powered outcomes trial.

Evidence runs opposite to a therapeutic claim: AGTR1 blockade by ARBs suppresses erythropoiesis (angiotensin II is a pro-erythropoietic growth factor and EPO secretagogue), and meta-analyses (e.g., QJM 2015) link ACEi/ARBs to CAUSING anemia/lowered hemoglobin; no trial uses azilsartan or any ARB to treat anemia, so this is a spurious genetic-ontology artifact reflecting a harmful, not beneficial, target-disease relationship.

BKM120 (buparlisib) was tested in multiple breast cancer trials including the phase III BELLE-2/BELLE-3 programs and a phase I with fulvestrant in ER+ metastatic breast cancer (PMC4818722, clinical benefit rate 58.6%) and a phase II in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (PMC7607628).

No BKM120 trial in autoimmune/immune disease, but the PIK3CD (p110delta) isoform that BKM120 hits is the immune isoform: same-class PI3Kdelta inhibitor leniolisib was FDA-approved (Mar 2023, NCT02435173 phase 3) for the inborn immune disorder APDS, and PI3Kdelta inhibitors are in development for lupus, RA and MS.

BKM120 is a pan-class I PI3K anticancer drug enrolled in 80+ oncology trials across glioblastoma (PMC4144634), recurrent/metastatic head and neck cancer (NCT01852292), and CNS lymphoma (NCT02301364), directly corroborating the broad 'cancer' term.

No clinical trial of BKM120 (or any PI3K inhibitor) treating hypertension; preclinical work (Cardiovasc Res 2012, academic.oup.com/cardiovascres/article/93/1/200) shows PI3Kgamma inhibition lowers blood pressure in hypertensive mice via an Akt/L-type calcium-channel vasorelaxant mechanism, though this is the gamma isoform, not the nominated PIK3CA/B/D primary targets.

BKM120 was trialed directly in ovarian cancer: a phase I of BKM120 + olaparib in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (29% ORR in 41 patients; Ann Oncol / NCT) and a phase Ib of BKM120 + trametinib showing 29% ORR in 21 ovarian cancer patients (Clin Cancer Res, PMID 25500057).

drug: DF2156A (ladarixin; Dompé oral dual CXCR1/CXCR2 allosteric antagonist)
evidence: No CXCR1/2-antagonist clinical trial in gastroenteritis/enterocolitis; but the selective CXCR2 antagonist SB225002 ameliorates acute experimental (DSS) colitis in mice (PMID 18653784), giving preclinical support for neutrophil-driven gut inflammation as a target-class indication. Ladarixin itself has no GI program.

drug: DF2156A (ladarixin; Dompé oral dual CXCR1/CXCR2 allosteric antagonist)
evidence: Strong preclinical/target-validation only: CXCR2 blockade (SB225002) markedly suppresses neutrophil proinflammatory activity and ameliorates DSS colitis (PMID 33042416), and CXCR1/CXCR2 were nominated as NET-related UC treatment targets via Mendelian randomization (Front Immunol 2024). No registered CXCR1/2-antagonist trial in UC (navarixin/reparixin/ladarixin have no IBD trial).

drug: DF2156A (ladarixin; Dompé oral dual CXCR1/CXCR2 allosteric antagonist)
evidence: PSC chemokine-receptor trials exist but target CCR2/CCR5 (cenicriviroc, PERSEUS/NCT02653625), not CXCR1/CXCR2; no clinical or specific preclinical CXCR1/2-antagonist evidence in PSC was found. Support is mechanistic (neutrophilic cholangitis) only.

drug: DF2156A (ladarixin; Dompé oral dual CXCR1/CXCR2 allosteric antagonist)
evidence: Same-target-class precedent: the CXCR2 antagonist SCH527123/navarixin ran a Phase II trial in psoriasis (NCT00688467), and the CXCR2 antagonist RIST4721 was tested in palmoplantar pustulosis (Phase 2, NCT05194839). Not ladarixin itself, but a clinical CXCR2 program in this indication exists.

drug: DF2156A (ladarixin; Dompé oral dual CXCR1/CXCR2 allosteric antagonist)
evidence: IL-8/CXCL8-neutrophil rationale is documented in AS (CD14+ monocytes overexpress CXCL8; shared neutrophil pathogenesis with IBD), but no CXCR1/2-antagonist clinical trial or AS-specific preclinical efficacy study was found; closest mechanistic data are from RA synovium, so support is target-rationale only.

Selective CXCR2 antagonist SB225002 ameliorates DSS- and TNBS-induced experimental colitis in mice (reduced neutrophil influx, MPO, IL-1beta); CXCR2 blockade suppresses neutrophil proinflammatory activity in human UC (PMC7540107, PMID 18653784). No registered CXCR2-antagonist clinical trial in UC/IBD found.

Only target rationale: IL-8/CXCL8 signals through CXCR1/CXCR2 to recruit neutrophils in H. pylori gastritis (PMC529101), but no CXCR2-antagonist preclinical efficacy study or clinical trial in gastroenteritis was found; H. pylori actually downregulates neutrophil CXCR2.

CXCR2 antagonism reduces neutrophil accumulation (CXCR2 immunohistochemistry) in the Mdr2-/- mouse model of sclerosing cholangitis, a preclinical PSC model (per CXCR2-antagonist liver-pathology literature, PMC9277870). No clinical trial of any CXCR2 antagonist in PSC found.

Only generic CXCL8-CXCR2 neutrophil-recruitment rationale; AS pathogenesis is dominated by IL-23/Th17/TNF and CXCR4 (osteogenic precursor migration), and no CXCR2-antagonist preclinical efficacy study or clinical trial in AS/spondyloarthritis was found.

Class precedent: the CXCR2 antagonist navarixin (SCH-527123/MK-7123) underwent Phase II evaluation in psoriasis, and RIST4721 (a CXCR2 antagonist) ran a Phase 2 study in palmoplantar pustulosis, a neutrophilic psoriasis variant (NCT05194839). No Danirixin-specific psoriasis trial exists.

No E6201 trial in HCM, but the same target class is in active clinical use: the MEK1/2 inhibitor trametinib is being tested in an RCT for RASopathy-associated HCM (NCT06555237, MEKinRAS, Medical Univ. Warsaw), and binimetinib/MEK162 was trialed in Noonan-syndrome HCM (NCT01556568), with published case reports of HCM reversal.

HCM is a cardiomyopathy; MEK1/2 inhibitors (trametinib, NCT06555237; binimetinib, NCT01556568) are in clinical trials for RAS/MAPK-pathway-driven cardiomyopathy, providing same-target-class clinical precedent though no E6201 trial exists.

Broad rollup term; the concrete cardiovascular program for this target class is MEK-inhibitor treatment of RASopathy hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (trametinib RCT NCT06555237), which reduces morbidity/mortality in children with RAS/MAPK-pathway cardiac disease.

MAP3K1 is a known sex-determination/gonadal-development gene and MEK1/2 signaling is essential for male fetal germline development (mouse studies, e.g. PMC10696798); MAPK/steroidogenesis links exist in Leydig cells, but no clinical or target-class trial of E6201 or any MEK inhibitor in hypogonadism was found.

E6201 itself was directly trialed as a topical gel for plaque-type psoriasis, an immune-mediated disease: Eisai-sponsored NCT00539929 (E6201 vs vehicle, plaque psoriasis) and NCT01268527 (topical E6201 gel in psoriasis vulgaris).

No Elafibranor RA trial exists (Elafibranor's clinical program is confined to liver disease: PBC/NASH/PSC). However the PPAR target class is in human RA trials: a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover RCT of the PPAR-gamma agonist pioglitazone 45 mg in RA (PMC3978636) showed reduced DAS28-CRP and CRP, and a second clinical study (PMC3040074) showed pioglitazone+methotrexate improved DAS28; the PPAR-alpha agonist fenofibrate (Elafibranor's exact PPARA target) reduced arthritis score in rat adjuvant-induced arthritis (PMID 24928921).

No Elafibranor or any PPAR-agonist clinical uveitis trial found, but Elafibranor's exact targets have preclinical efficacy: the PPAR-alpha agonist fenofibrate ameliorated experimental autoimmune uveoretinitis in Lewis rats (Mol Vis 2014, PMC4225135) and the PPAR-gamma agonist pioglitazone suppressed experimental autoimmune uveitis (PMID 24107513).

No Elafibranor trial and no PPAR-agonist clinical trial in celiac disease (the celiac clinical pipeline centers on larazotide, an unrelated tight-junction agent). Mechanistic/preclinical link only: gliadin p31-43 induces tissue-transglutaminase-mediated PPAR-gamma downregulation in celiac mucosa and PPAR signaling is implicated in celiac tissue damage (Mol Med 2010, PMC2864807), with PPAR ligands anti-inflammatory in rodent intestinal models.

No Elafibranor or PPAR-agonist clinical trial in ankylosing spondylitis. PPAR-gamma is reported as an NF-kB inhibitor implicated in AS inflammatory pathways, and PPAR-alpha agonist fenofibrate has anti-arthritic/anti-inflammatory preclinical effects in arthritis rodent models (PMC3681315, AJP-Endo 2011); evidence is mechanistic/preclinical with no AS-specific trial.

No trial of elenbecestat or any BACE1 inhibitor exists for hyperlipidemia (the class is Alzheimer's-only; elenbecestat program NCT02956486/NCT03036280 was early-AD, halted 2019). Preclinical-only link: BACE1-/- mice are lean, protected from diet-induced obesity, insulin-sensitized and excrete less fecal lipid (Meakin et al., Biochem J 2011; 'BACE1: more than just a beta-secretase', Obesity Reviews 2022), supporting a broad metabolic/lipid-handling role but no clinical evidence.

No elenbecestat or BACE1-inhibitor trial in hypercholesterolemia, and the cholesterol-specific preclinical evidence is null: BACE1-/- mice show NO difference in serum cholesterol (Meakin et al. 2011) and the literature states 'BACE1 is not involved in apoE and cholesterol metabolism' (cholesterol is normal in BACE1 KO; gamma-secretase/APP-LRP1 governs that axis). Only the genetic/mechanistic rationale (BACE1 co-localizes with cholesterol in lipid rafts; serum BACE1 activity weakly correlates with lower HDL) supports the nomination.

Beraprost (the prostacyclin-analog racemate of which esuberaprost is the active 314d isomer) pretreatment prevented stress-induced gastric mucosal erosions in rats (ScienceDirect S0024320599001411), and IP-receptor knockout mouse studies (PubMed 11595421) show endogenous prostacyclin/IP signaling is gastroprotective against mucosal injury; no registered clinical trial of esuberaprost or any IP agonist in gastroenteritis/GI mucosal inflammation was found.

PGI2 alleviates DSS-induced colitis by reducing intestinal epithelial permeability/apoptosis and a PGI2 defect is present in IBD-patient mucosa (CMGH 2021, PMC8342971), and a PTGIR agonist reversed intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's disease in vivo (J Crohn's Colitis 2025, jjaf084); IP-receptor-agonist patents name UC/Crohn's as indications, but no registered/completed clinical trial of esuberaprost or any IP-receptor agonist in ulcerative colitis was found.

Etavopivat (FT-4202), a PKR/PKLR allosteric activator, is in registered trials for the anemias of sickle cell disease and thalassemia, including Phase 2 GLADIOLUS (NCT04987489) and Phase 3 HIBISCUS, which met both co-primary endpoints (hemoglobin response 48.7% vs 7.2% placebo).

No trial of etavopivat or any PK activator targets gout, but the disease etavopivat treats (chronic hemolytic anemia, e.g. sickle cell) is a documented cause of secondary hyperuricemia and gout via increased erythrocyte purine turnover (clinical case-report literature, e.g. tophaceous gout in autoimmune/sickle-cell hemolytic anemia); the link is to the hemolysis, not a direct anti-gout mechanism.

No PKLR/etavopivat lung program; the pyruvate-kinase link to lung fibrosis is via the different isoform PKM2 (PKM2 stabilizes TGF-beta1 receptor I and promotes bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, Science Advances 2022). PKLR is the liver/erythrocyte isoform and is not the fibrosis-implicated isoform, so this is isoform-family preclinical signal only.

No PKLR-bipolar trial, drug, or specific gene association found; bipolar metabolic literature implicates the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and pyruvate carboxylase / mitochondrial dysfunction (elevated brain pyruvate/lactate), not pyruvate kinase PKLR. Only a thin generic glycolysis/brain-energy rationale supports it (consistent with the low 0.385 genetic score), likely an ontology roll-up artifact.

No dedicated evacetrapib metabolic-syndrome trial exists; CETP inhibitors as a class affect glucose/insulin metabolism (systematic review/meta-analysis of CETP inhibitors on new-onset diabetes, Eur Heart J Cardiovasc Pharmacother 2022 8:622), and new-onset diabetes was tracked as a secondary outcome in evacetrapib's ACCELERATE and anacetrapib's REVEAL, but no CETP-inhibitor program targets metabolic syndrome as a registered indication.

Evacetrapib was developed and clinically trialed specifically for dyslipidemia/hyperlipidemia: the Phase II RCT (Nicholls et al., JAMA 2011;306:2099, NCT01105975) tested evacetrapib as monotherapy and with statins in patients with elevated LDL-C/low HDL-C, producing up to +128% HDL-C and -35% LDL-C.

No evacetrapib COVID-19 trial exists, but the same-target-class CETP inhibitor dalcetrapib was tested in the dal-COVID Phase 2a randomized trial (NCT04676867) in mild-to-moderate COVID-19, based on dalcetrapib binding and inhibiting the SARS-CoV-2 3CL main protease (Pelletier et al., 2021).

Evacetrapib was directly trialed in coronary/vascular disease: the Phase 3 ACCELERATE trial (Lincoff et al., NEJM 2017;376:1933, NCT01687998) enrolled 12,092 high-risk vascular patients including those with acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery disease with diabetes (trial stopped early for lack of efficacy).

No ezutromid or other utrophin (UTRN) modulator trial in schizophrenia exists. UTRN does appear in psychiatric genetics literature, but the prominent UTRN GWAS hit (rs9390170, Psychiatry Investig) is for restless legs syndrome, not schizophrenia; UTRN is not among the 120 prioritised genes in the PGC3 schizophrenia GWAS (Trubetskoy et al., Nature 2022). The 0.633 score appears to be a genetic-ontology rollup with no clinical, preclinical, or target-class precedent in schizophrenia.

No ezutromid or other utrophin-modulator clinical or preclinical program targets chronic pain. UTRN's documented role is structural (neuromuscular junction membrane maintenance and acetylcholine-receptor clustering); no literature links utrophin modulation to analgesia. The 0.528 score rests only on the genetic/target rationale with no clinical, preclinical, or class evidence found.

Ezutromid (SMT C1100) was developed specifically for DMD and tested in the Phase 2 open-label PhaseOut DMD trial (NCT02858362) in ambulatory boys with DMD; 38 patients completed 48 weeks. The trial failed its primary endpoint (June 2018) and Summit discontinued development, but a direct, registered clinical trial of this drug in this indication exists.

Muscular dystrophy is the parent term for the indication ezutromid was actually trialed in: the Phase 2 PhaseOut DMD study (NCT02858362) of ezutromid in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (a muscular dystrophy). A clinically equivalent registered trial of this drug exists.

GSK2586184 was discontinued ~2014, before COVID-19 existed, so it was never trialed in COVID-19; but the JAK inhibitor baricitinib received FDA EUA (Nov 2020) and full FDA approval (May 2022) for hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring oxygen, establishing JAK-pathway (incl. JAK1/IL-6 cytokine-storm) class precedent in this indication.

GSK2586184 itself was studied in Phase 2 trials for the immune-mediated diseases systemic lupus erythematosus (halted for futility plus liver-enzyme elevations/DRESS), chronic plaque psoriasis (met PASI75 primary endpoint, 62% vs 0% placebo at 400 mg), and ulcerative colitis (case reports, PMC5624036) — the broad immune-system-disease term resolves to real direct programs of this drug.

No record of GSK2586184 itself in RA, but same-class selective JAK1 inhibitors upadacitinib (Rinvoq) and filgotinib are FDA/EMA-approved for rheumatoid arthritis on the strength of Phase III trials (PMC8098104), giving strong selective-JAK1 target-class approval precedent.

No clinical trial of GSK2798745 or any TRPV4 inhibitor in gout exists (GSK2798745's registered program is heart failure/pulmonary edema, e.g. NCT02119260/NCT02497937; registered gout pipeline trials are NLRP3 inhibitor dapansutrile NCT05658575 and URAT1 inhibitor ABP-671, not TRPV4). However, strong preclinical support: a 2022 study (PMC9131364) shows macrophage TRPV4 is required for monosodium-urate-crystal-induced inflammation via NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and the selective TRPV4 antagonist GSK219 reduced joint swelling, leukocyte infiltration, MPO, IL-1beta and pain in a mouse gout model, comparable to colchicine.

No Ganetespib or other HSP90-inhibitor trial/approval exists for gout (clinical HSP90 inhibitors are anticancer only), but the HSP90 target class has preclinical anti-inflammatory/autoimmune disease evidence including Ganetespib itself ameliorating disease in the MRL/lpr lupus mouse model (PMC4431681) and HSP90 inhibitors active in rheumatoid arthritis models (PubMed 19035474); mechanistically HSP90 chaperones the NLRP3 inflammasome/IL-1beta axis that drives monosodium-urate gout inflammation. No gout-specific (MSU-crystal) HSP90-inhibitor study was found — the direct crystal-inflammasome heat-shock link in the literature is HSP60, not HSP90 (PMC7791970) — so the gout connection is mechanistic/class-extrapolative, not a demonstrated gout program.

Idasanutlin + atezolizumab was tested in metastatic colorectal cancer (a digestive-system cancer) in the Morpheus-CRC trial NCT03555149, and the idasanutlin Phase I solid-tumor study enrolled 12 colorectal cancer patients.

No idasanutlin-specific head/neck trial found, but same-target-class MDM2 inhibitor APG-115 (alrizomadlin) ran a Phase 1/2 trial in p53-wildtype salivary gland (head and neck) cancers with reported monotherapy antitumor activity (notably in adenoid cystic carcinoma).

Idasanutlin was administered (orally Days 1-5, combined with atezolizumab) in metastatic colorectal cancer in Morpheus-CRC NCT03555149; the Phase I solid-tumor study also enrolled 12 (12.1%) colorectal cancer patients.

Sarcoma was the most-enrolled tumor type (23 patients, 23.2%) in the idasanutlin Phase I solid-tumor study (PMC8541972), including liposarcoma, with two sarcoma patients showing prolonged stable disease >600 days and responses reported in liposarcoma.

No idasanutlin-specific HCC clinical trial confirmed; preclinical studies show MDM2-p53 antagonists including RG7388/Nutlin-3 exert antitumor effects in wild-type-p53 HCC cells (~75% of HCC is TP53-wildtype), supporting target rationale but not a registered HCC trial of the drug.

Iferanserin itself has only ever been trialed for hemorrhoids (NCT01483833 Phase 2; NCT01355874 Phase 3, terminated) as a peripherally-acting intra-anal 5-HT2A antagonist, with no CNS/psychiatric program. However the HTR2A target class has extensive clinical psychiatric precedent: pimavanserin (selective 5-HT2A antagonist/inverse agonist) is approved for Parkinson's disease psychosis and ran Phase 3 in MDD, and 5-HT2A-antagonist atypical antipsychotics (risperidone, quetiapine, brexpiprazole) are widely used across mental/behavioural disorders. Broad ontology roll-up term, but a real target-class clinical footprint exists.

No Iferanserin MDD trial exists (drug is hemorrhoid-only, peripherally acting). Same-target precedent is strong: pimavanserin, a 5-HT2A antagonist/inverse agonist, completed a positive Phase 2 (CLARITY) and ran Phase 3 trials (NCT03968159, NCT03999918) as adjunctive treatment for MDD; mirtazapine/trazodone/agomelatine also carry 5-HT2A antagonism with antidepressant use.

No Iferanserin OCD trial. Target-class precedent: 5-HT2A-antagonist atypical antipsychotics (risperidone, brexpiprazole, aripiprazole) are established evidence-based SSRI-augmentation agents in treatment-resistant OCD (meta-analyses of double-blind RCTs), with 5-HT2A blockade proposed as a contributing mechanism.

No Iferanserin anxiety trial. Target-class precedent: quetiapine and risperidone (5-HT2A antagonists) have RCT evidence in generalized anxiety disorder including as adjuncts to SSRIs (e.g., quetiapine GAD trials; risperidone vs paroxetine NCT00457106), and the 5-HT2A receptor is mechanistically implicated in amygdala/hypothalamic anxiety circuits; trifluoperazine (a 5-HT2A-blocking antipsychotic) is FDA-approved for anxiety.

No itacitinib COVID-19 trial found, but the same-target-class JAK1/2 inhibitor baricitinib (Olumiant, co-developed by Incyte/Lilly) received full FDA approval on May 11, 2022 for hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring oxygen support, and ruxolitinib (JAK1/2) was trialed for COVID-19 cytokine storm (e.g., RUXCOVID NCT04362137).

Broad ontology rollup is backed by multiple real itacitinib programs in immune-mediated disease: acute GVHD Phase 3 GRAVITAS-301 (NCT03139604), chronic GVHD GRAVITAS-309 (NCT03584516), and bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome after lung/HCT transplant (NCT03978637, NCT04239989).

Completed Incyte Phase 2 trial NCT01626573 ('Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of Itacitinib in Subjects With Active Rheumatoid Arthritis') showed significant ACR20/50/70 and DAS28-CRP improvement vs placebo; RA development was later deprioritized in favor of hematology/oncology.

Directionality is inverted: DGAT1 loss-of-function (homozygous mutations) CAUSES severe congenital watery diarrhea with protein-losing enteropathy, and the DGAT1 inhibitor pradigastat (LCQ908) itself CAUSES diarrhea as its dose-limiting adverse event (53.3-71.4% incidence at 20-40mg vs 33.3% placebo in the 52-week FCS trial). No LCQ908 or DGAT1-inhibitor-class trial treats diarrhea; the genetic 0.927 score is a real DGAT1-diarrhea ontology link but with reversed therapeutic direction (inhibiting the target produces, not treats, the disease).

Multiple registered trials of LY3023414 in breast cancer exist: NCT04032080 (LY3023414 + prexasertib in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, 25% PR / 37.5% SD), plus a Phase 1b combination with fulvestrant in treatment-refractory advanced breast cancer (ASCO JCO 2017, 56% disease control rate) and combinations with abemaciclib/letrozole.

LY3023414 is a clinical-stage pan-cancer oncology drug; first-in-human Phase 1 study NCT01655225 (A Study of LY3023414 in Participants With Advanced Cancer, Clin Cancer Res 2018, PMID 29636360) enrolled advanced solid tumors with tumor-specific expansion cohorts (mesothelioma, breast, NHL, squamous NSCLC).

NCT03675893 'Letrozole and Abemaciclib and LY3023414 in Ovarian Cancer and Endometrial Cancer' is a registered trial of LY3023414 in low-grade serous ovarian cancer; additionally LY3023414 + prexasertib was tested in high-grade serous ovarian cancer models with a supporting Phase 1b trial (NCT02124148).

No LY3214996 cardiovascular trial exists (its program is oncology-only: pancreatic NCT04386057, melanoma/CRC/AML, RASopathy-tumor basket NCT04534283). For the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK class, evidence is preclinical/mechanistic only: ERK1/2 inhibition reduced vascular calcification via miR-126-3p-DKK1/LRP6 (PMC7738895) and reviews (Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMC11247000) describe MEK/ERK inhibitors as 'promising' for atherosclerosis/CVD in animal models, while warning of cardiotoxicity risk; no human CVD trial of an ERK or MEK inhibitor for general cardiovascular disease was found.

A drug in the same RAS-MAPK cascade (trametinib, a MEK1/2 inhibitor one node upstream of the ERK1/2 target) is in a registered Phase 2 trial for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in RASopathies (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06555237) and is documented in published off-label clinical use reversing myocardial hypertrophy in Noonan/RAF1-related cardiomyopathy (JACC 2019, PMID 38827265). LY3214996 itself (the ERK1/2 inhibitor) has no cardiomyopathy trial; class precedent is via MEK, not direct ERK1/2 inhibition.

Same-cascade MEK1/2 inhibitor trametinib has a registered Phase 2 RCT specifically for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in RASopathy patients (NCT06555237, ~40 patients, 12-month trametinib vs standard therapy) plus multiple published treated cases (e.g. RAF1-related obstructive HCM, PMID 38827265). No direct LY3214996/ERK1/2-inhibitor HCM trial; the clinical precedent is MEK inhibition in the identical RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK pathway that drives cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.

ESR2 appears as a susceptibility locus in some AF meta-analyses, but the validated lone-AF genetic signal is to ESR1/ER-alpha (TA-repeat polymorphism, PMC3944416), not ESR2; no ESR2/ERbeta-agonist clinical trial or AF-specific preclinical intervention study was found — only general (non-AF) anti-fibrotic ERbeta data.

LY500307 itself was run in a placebo-controlled depression trial, NCT03689543 ('Effects of an ER Beta Agonist (Lilly Compound LY500307) on Estradiol-Withdrawal-Induced Mood Symptoms in Women With Past Perimenopausal Depression'), and an adjunctive schizophrenia trial (NCT01874756) also targeted mood/negative symptoms.

Multiple preclinical heart-failure studies show ERbeta agonists are cardioprotective — the ERbeta agonist DPN (not the ERalpha agonist PPT) improved ejection fraction to ~45% in HF mice and reversed contractile dysfunction/fibrosis (Biol Sex Differ 2018, PMC6208048; PMC9308745) — but no clinical trial of LY500307 or any ESR2 drug exists in DCM/cardiomyopathy.

No clinical trial of Lanabecestat or any BACE1 inhibitor exists for hyperlipidemia (all BACE1 inhibitor programs, including Lanabecestat trials AMARANTH/NCT02245737 and DAYBREAK-ALZ/NCT02783573, targeted only Alzheimer's disease), but preclinical literature ties the target to lipid metabolism: BACE1 is elevated in oxLDL-driven macrophage foam cells and its knockdown reduces lipid droplet accumulation (Taylor 2022, Obesity Reviews 'BACE1: More than just a beta-secretase'), and BACE1 knock-in mice show increased plasma lipid accumulation and a metabolic/diabetes phenotype.

No registered clinical trial of Lanabecestat or any other BACE1 inhibitor exists for hypercholesterolemia, and Lanabecestat is unapproved (discontinued June 2018), so no off-label use. However preclinical/mechanistic literature links BACE1 to cholesterol biology: lipid-raft cholesterol regulates BACE1-mediated APP cleavage and BACE1 clustering, and BACE1 contributes to oxLDL-driven foam-cell formation relevant to atherogenic cholesterol handling (Taylor 2022 Obesity Reviews review of BACE1 in lipid metabolism).

Enpatoran (M5049), the TLR7/8 inhibitor, is in registered clinical trials across multiple immune-mediated/autoimmune diseases beyond lupus: the Phase 2 NEPTUNIA trial (NCT05650567) in dermatomyositis/polymyositis, plus prior development in COVID-19 immune-mediated pneumonia. The broad 'immune system disease' roll-up maps directly onto enpatoran's documented autoimmune clinical program.

Enpatoran (M5049) was tested directly in SLE: the Phase 2 WILLOW basket study (NCT05162586) included a moderate-to-severe SLE cohort (Cohort B, reported in The Lancet 2026) and a long-term extension (NCT05540327), preceded by Phase Ib NCT04647708 in active SLE/CLE.

Motesanib diphosphate was tested in a registered phase 2 trial in progressive differentiated thyroid cancer (Sherman et al., NEJM 2008, 93 patients, ORR 14%, DCR 81%) and a separate phase 2 trial in advanced/metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (Schlumberger et al., J Clin Oncol 2009).

No motesanib trial exists for endometriosis, but same-target-class VEGFR/anti-angiogenic agents (sorafenib targeting VEGFR-2/RAF, bevacizumab) significantly reduce endometriotic implant volume in rodent xenograft models (e.g., PubMed 26169036; PLOS One 2016 meta-analysis pone.0166658). However, reviews explicitly note NO human clinical trials of anti-VEGF/VEGFR agents in endometriosis have been conducted, so the precedent is preclinical/target-class only, not a registered clinical program.

RO5285119 is balovaptan, a selective vasopressin V1a (AVPR1A) antagonist (Roche, tested clinically only in autism). The V1a receptor is expressed in bladder detrusor smooth muscle and renal medulla, where V1a activation drives detrusor contraction, and preclinical work shows V1a-receptor blockade reduces the micturition-reflex threshold pressure in female rats (PMC9525731), giving a direct mechanistic/animal link to lower urinary tract control. However, no registered clinical trial of balovaptan exists in any urinary indication (urinary frequency/pollakiuria appears only as an adverse event in the ASD trials, e.g. NCT02901431), it has no urinary approval/off-label use, and the V1a-selective prototype relcovaptan (SR49059) was never trialed for a urinary disease (its programs were in preterm labor, dysmenorrhea, Raynaud's; phase II discontinued). The approved vasopressin urology drugs (desmopressin, VA106483) target the V2 receptor, not V1a, so they are not same-target precedent. Corroboration is therefore preclinical/mechanistic, not clinical.

No reparixin UC trial exists (ClinicalTrials.gov API confirms reparixin's portfolio is breast cancer, myelofibrosis, transplant/IRI, COVID/ARDS, islet transplant only), but the same-class CXCR2 antagonist SB-656933 (GSK) was clinically tested in ulcerative colitis to reduce neutrophil accumulation in the colon (NCT00748410, Phase 2, terminated); strong preclinical support also exists (selective CXCR2 antagonist SB225002 ameliorated DSS/TNBS experimental colitis).

No reparixin psoriasis trial exists, but the same-class dual CXCR1/CXCR2 antagonist navarixin (SCH 527123 / MK-7123) was run in a Phase II psoriasis study (development stopped for lack of efficacy); RIST4721 (CXCR2 antagonist) also reached Phase 2 in the related neutrophilic skin disease palmoplantar pustulosis, confirming an active CXCR2-targeting clinical program in inflammatory skin disease.

Rilzabrutinib (Wayrilz, Sanofi) was FDA-approved Aug 29, 2025 for adults with persistent/chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) based on the pivotal Phase 3 LUNA 3 trial, and has active trials in other immune-mediated diseases (IgG4-related disease Phase 2b, chronic spontaneous urticaria RILECSU Phase 2 which met its primary endpoint, and moderate-to-severe asthma Phase 2) — ITP and these conditions are immune system diseases, so the drug is approved/in direct trials for this indication.

No SAR439859 OA trial exists, but the same target (ESR1) is clinically pursued in OA: the HOPE-e randomized placebo-controlled feasibility RCT tested conjugated estrogens plus the SERM bazedoxifene in postmenopausal women with symptomatic hand osteoarthritis (Watt et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2022), and a raloxifene RCT relieved knee OA pain. Note directionality caveat: OA benefit comes from ER agonism/SERMs, whereas amcenestrant is an ER degrader/antagonist (opposite pharmacology).

Same target (ESR1) has clinical programs in arthritis: the ER-alpha agonist Org 37663 was tested in a Phase IIa RCT in postmenopausal rheumatoid arthritis patients (PubMed 20112368), and SERMs bazedoxifene/raloxifene have RA RCTs (e.g., bazedoxifene in glucocorticoid-treated RA, Arthritis Res Ther 2021). No SAR439859 arthritis trial; same directionality caveat (amcenestrant is a SERD/antagonist, arthritis benefit is from ER agonism).

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01688973 ('Tivantinib With or Without Erlotinib Hydrochloride in Treating Patients With Metastatic or Locally Advanced Kidney Cancer That Cannot Be Removed by Surgery') is a registered phase II trial of tivantinib in papillary renal cell carcinoma, a kidney cancer.

NCT01688973 is a randomized phase II trial assessing response rate and PFS of tivantinib (ARQ 197) with or without erlotinib specifically in patients with locally advanced or metastatic papillary renal cell carcinoma.

Tivantinib was studied in multiple digestive-system cancers, including two phase III hepatocellular carcinoma trials (METIV-HCC, JET-HCC; e.g., NCT01755767) and a phase II trial in MET-high KRAS-wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer combined with cetuximab (NCT01892527), plus gastric cancer in phase I.

Abemaciclib has registered/completed melanoma trials: the phase I trial (Patnaik et al., Cancer Discovery 2016) included a 26-patient melanoma cohort (1 RECIST partial response, disease control rate 27%), and NCT02308020 enrolled a dedicated melanoma cohort (23 patients) for brain metastases.

The melanoma cohorts in abemaciclib trials (Patnaik phase I, NCT02308020) were predominantly cutaneous melanoma (the dominant subtype enriched for NRAS/INK4 alterations driving aberrant CDK4/6 activity); CDK4/6 inhibitors are also in BRAF/MEK combination trials specifically for cutaneous BRAF-V600 melanoma (e.g., encorafenib+binimetinib+ribociclib).

No abemaciclib (or any CDK4/6-inhibitor) epilepsy trial exists; the genetic epilepsy-CDK signal in literature maps to CDK5 and CDKL5 (CDKL5-deficiency disorder causes epilepsy) — a different kinase family, indicating a likely CDK name-family genetic-ontology roll-up rather than a CDK4/6-specific link.

Same-target-class muscarinic M2/M3 antagonists (solifenacin, tolterodine) are in phase 3 trials and clinical use for BPH-associated storage LUTS (NEPTUNE trial, n=1,334, solifenacin+tamsulosin); however atropine itself is contraindicated in BPH because nonselective antimuscarinic action worsens urinary retention (StatPearls), so the genetic target link is real but the effect direction for atropine is unfavorable.

Atropine and atropine-like anticholinergics have documented obstetric use: Hirsch (1937) reported intrapartum administration of an atropine-like drug (Syntropan) shortened labor, and the antispasmodic/anticholinergic class is in modern RCTs for labor augmentation/cervical dilatation (rociverine, hyoscine butylbromide); atropine itself is used clinically in pregnancy when indicated (vagolytic/antisialagogue, crosses placenta) per UKTIS and the FDA atropine sulfate label.

No registered clinical trial of azacitidine in dementia/Alzheimer's exists, but DNMT inhibitors including azacitidine (5-azacytidine) and decitabine show neuroprotection in preclinical Huntingtin and Alzheimer's N2a/APPswe cellular and mouse models, and a USPTO patent (US10842807) covers 'Methods of treating neurodegenerative disorders comprising DNA methyltransferase inhibitors' — mechanistic plausibility supported preclinically, no clinical program.

Azacitidine (Vidaza) is FDA-approved for multiple hematopoietic neoplasms (MDS subtypes RA/RARS/RAEB/RAEB-T, CMML, JMML) and EU-approved for AML; direct trials in this exact disease space include NCT04752163 ('Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Cell Neoplasm' with azacitidine) and the ORACLE phase 3 study of oral azacitidine in follicular helper T-cell lymphoma.

Danicopan (Voydeya) is FDA-approved as add-on therapy for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), an immune/complement-mediated hemolytic disease driven by alternative-pathway dysregulation, and was directly trialed in the complement/immune-complex-mediated kidney disease C3 glomerulopathy/IC-MPGN (NCT03124368, two Phase 2 studies). The CFD/Factor D target class regulates the alternative complement pathway, a core innate/adaptive immune effector, so this broad ontology term maps to real registered danicopan programs in complement-mediated immune disease.

No clinical trial of eFT508 or any MNK1/2 inhibitor exists for carpal tunnel syndrome (all registered eFT508 trials are oncology, e.g. NCT03616834, NCT03690141), and no CTS-specific study was found; however, eFT508 (tomivosertib) is shown to suppress ectopic spontaneous activity in human dorsal root ganglion nociceptors from neuropathic-pain dermatomes (PMC10312735; Brain 2024, PMID 39046204) and MNK1/2-eIF4E signaling drives injury-induced nociceptor sensitization/chronic neuropathic pain (PMC5546114), providing preclinical/mechanistic target-class linkage to the neuropathic-pain disease area that encompasses the symptomatic burden of carpal tunnel (a focal compression neuropathy) but no clinical or CTS-specific evidence.

No galeterone CAH trial exists, but abiraterone (same CYP17A1-inhibitor target class) is in registered CAH trials NCT02574910 ('Androgen Reduction in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, Phase 1') and NCT03548246 (hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone + abiraterone in CAH), with published Phase 1 data showing androstenedione fell from 764 to 254 ng/dL on 100 mg/day; CYP17A1 inhibition reduces the androgen excess of classic 21-OHD CAH.

Galeterone itself was directly developed and clinically trialed in prostate cancer: ARMOR2 Phase 2 (NCT01709734) and the ARMOR3-SV Phase 3 randomized trial of galeterone vs enzalutamide in AR-V7+ metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (PMID 31542304); 'familial' is a genetic-ontology subtype of the same prostate-cancer disease the drug was directly tested in.

Genetic-ontology link is real (CYP17A1 and AR are required for spermatogenesis; CYP17A1 haploinsufficiency CAUSES male infertility, PMID 15890676), but directionality is backwards: galeterone inhibits CYP17A1 and degrades/antagonizes AR, which would suppress androgens and worsen fertility — it is a cause/contraindication, not a treatment. No galeterone or target-class trial, off-label use, or therapeutic preclinical support for treating infertility was found.

NCT03481842 (Phase I, UniversitatsSpital Zurich, 94 endometriosis patients, 2018) tested vaginal anti-angiogenic suppositories that explicitly include linifanib (ABT-869) alongside axitinib and afatinib for treatment of genital endometriosis.

Mendelian-randomization study (Sjaarda et al., JACC 2018;72:300-310) found CSF1 - the ligand of linifanib's primary target CSF1R - is a causal mediator of CAD (OR 1.18 per SD, p=2.1e-4), supported by preclinical work showing CSF1R-driven macrophage/foam-cell formation in atherosclerotic plaque; however no clinical trial of linifanib or any CSF1R-axis inhibitor for CAD treatment was found, and CSF1R inhibition can impair post-MI cardiac recovery.

Lumateperone (Caplyta) was FDA-approved on Nov 6, 2025 as adjunctive therapy for MDD, supported by two positive Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials (Study 501 and Study 502; e.g., 4.9-point MADRS improvement vs placebo, effect size 0.61) in adults with inadequate antidepressant response.

Lumateperone is FDA-approved (2021) for depressive episodes in bipolar I/II disorder as monotherapy and adjunct; Phase 3 monotherapy trial NCT02600494 met its primary endpoint (MADRS p<0.001, effect size 0.56).

No lumateperone trial targets anxiety disorder as a primary indication (only secondary anxious-distress/inner-tension item improvement in depression Study 403, NCT04285515), but the same DRD2/HTR2A target class has GAD clinical-trial/use evidence, e.g., quetiapine in randomized GAD augmentation trials (NCT00113295, NCT00229645) and a low-dose quetiapine GAD meta-analysis.

Salsalate, a salicylate of the same anti-inflammatory class as 5-ASA, was tested in multiple T2D RCTs (TINSAL-T2D, n=286: HbA1c 0.37% lower vs placebo over 48 weeks, PMID 23817699), and PPARG is the direct target of approved thiazolidinedione antidiabetics; a retrospective study of 6,197 UC+metabolic-syndrome patients also found oral mesalamine significantly decreased fasting glucose (P<0.001) over 12 months, but no registered RCT of mesalamine as a primary diabetes therapy exists.

ALOX5 (5-lipoxygenase) is the direct target of zileuton, the first FDA-approved (1996) 5-LOX inhibitor indicated for chronic asthma, and the same leukotriene pathway underlies approved montelukast/zafirlukast; for mesalamine itself only preclinical support exists (5-ASA attenuated allergen-induced airway inflammation in an OVA mouse asthma model, PMID 25101553), with no registered human asthma trial of mesalamine found.

NCT03925350 is a single-arm Phase II investigator-initiated trial of single-agent niraparib in advanced/metastatic melanoma with homologous-recombination pathway mutations; 14 patients, 2 confirmed responses and disease control rate 64% (published JCO Precision Oncology PO-24-00658, 2025). A second niraparib trial (NCT03207347, UF-STO-ETI-001) covers BAP1/DDR-deficient neoplasms including melanoma.

The same niraparib Phase II trial NCT03925350 enrolled 'nonuveal metastatic melanoma' (i.e., predominantly cutaneous melanoma, excluding uveal), directly corroborating the cutaneous-melanoma nomination; cutaneous melanoma is the dominant non-uveal subtype with ~21-34% harboring HR-pathway aberrations. Target-class precedent also exists (olaparib, talazoparib in melanoma trials).

Pacritinib has registered clinical trials in graft-versus-host disease (an immune-mediated disease): NCT02891603 (Phase I/II GVHD prevention with sirolimus/tacrolimus, completed, final Phase 2 results published in Blood 2024, 144:2295) and NCT05531786 (Phase I/II in refractory chronic GVHD), driven by its JAK2/IRAK1/CSF1R immunomodulatory activity.

Pacritinib (Vonjo) is FDA-approved (Feb 28, 2022) for intermediate/high-risk myelofibrosis with thrombocytopenia (a hematopoietic/myeloid neoplasm), and was studied clinically in AML (n=7, Phase 1/2 myeloid malignancy study, PMC5146859) and in relapsed lymphoma (SB1518 Phase I study showing activity across multiple lymphoma subtypes), directly covering both the hematopoietic and lymphoid arms of this indication.

Parsaclisib has registered/completed clinical trials in primary warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (an immune system disease): a phase 2 open-label study (NCT05073458 / sponsor ID INCB 50465-309; published Barcellini et al., Am J Hematol 2024, doi:10.1002/ajh.27493, 64% PR/CR response) and a randomized phase 3 trial (PATHWAY); additional autoimmune-mechanism work exists in experimental pemphigoid disease.

The FGFR1-hypogonadism link is real but mechanistically REVERSED: congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism / Kallmann syndrome is caused by LOSS-OF-FUNCTION FGFR1 mutations (KAL2, ~10% of KS cases; e.g. R254W, V429E), so an FGFR inhibitor like pemigatinib would further impair FGFR1 signaling and worsen, not treat, the condition (PMC5463295; PMC6994936 shows FGFR inhibition reduces germ cell survival in fetal gonads). This is a spurious genetic-ontology artifact - high genetic score from a strong gene-disease association that points the wrong way for an antagonist. No trial, no class precedent, evidence against.

The phase 2 FIGHT-207 basket trial of pemigatinib in FGFR1-3-altered solid tumors (NCT03822117; Nat Med 2024, PMID 38710951) explicitly reported activity in cervical cancer among the tumor types responding, directly treating this drug in this indication (cervical cancer harbors recurrent FGFR2/FGFR3 alterations).

Pemigatinib was tested directly in metastatic FGF/FGFR-altered colorectal cancer in the ACCRU-GI-1701 phase II single-arm trial (NCT04096417) and a second multicenter phase II (NCT05202236, gastric/colorectal); a registered/completed trial of this exact drug in this indication exists, though ACCRU-GI-1701 closed for futility (0% ORR, n=14 interim) - so corroboration is 'field is pursuing it' but the clinical result was negative.

Rivaroxaban (Xarelto) is FDA-approved for treatment of DVT/PE and reduction of recurrent VTE, for extended VTE treatment (10 mg once daily after >=6 months therapy), and for VTE prevention in hospitalized acutely ill medical patients; validated in the EINSTEIN clinical trial programme (e.g., EINSTEIN-DVT/EXT) and FDA-approved Nov 2012.

The EINSTEIN-PE trial (NEJM 2012, n~4,833 symptomatic PE patients) showed oral rivaroxaban non-inferior to enoxaparin/VKA standard therapy with lower major bleeding; rivaroxaban is FDA-approved (Nov 2012) and EMA-approved specifically for treatment of acute pulmonary embolism.

A completed phase II trial of rucaparib (PF-01367338/AG014699) plus temozolomide in 46 chemotherapy-naive patients with metastatic melanoma showed chemopotentiation and improved PFS over historical temozolomide-alone controls (PubMed 23423489; Pfizer trials A4991002/A4991005).

The same rucaparib + temozolomide phase II metastatic melanoma trial (PubMed 23423489) enrolled chemotherapy-naive metastatic melanoma patients, a population that is overwhelmingly cutaneous melanoma; PARP-inhibitor melanoma literature specifically frames cutaneous melanoma BRCA/DNA-repair mutations (~11.5% of cutaneous melanoma) as the rationale, making cutaneous melanoma a clearly equivalent disease term to the registered rucaparib trial.

A registered clinical trial of selinexor in CLL exists: NCT02303392 (Selinexor and Ibrutinib in Treating Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia or Aggressive Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma); selinexor also showed antitumor activity in CLL patients in the phase 1 trial NCT01607892.

Karyopharm ran a Phase 1 trial of selinexor (KPT-330) in pediatric relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia and AML (NCT02091245), and the SELHEM trial NCT02212561 tested selinexor with fludarabine and cytarabine in relapsed/refractory acute leukemia including ALL.

NCT04187833 is a registered Phase II trial of talazoparib combined with nivolumab in patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma harboring BRCA/BRCAness (HRR) mutations (Cleveland Clinic, sponsored by Pfizer); results presented at AACR 2024 (Abstract CT261) and ASCO 2020 (TPS10082).

The same talazoparib+nivolumab Phase II trial (NCT04187833) explicitly enrolled cutaneous melanoma patients (3 of the reported cohort), alongside blue-nevus and uveal melanoma subtypes, all with DNA-repair gene mutations (BAP1, BRCA2, ATM, ATR, ARID2).

No valbenazine, VMAT2-class (tetrabenazine/deutetrabenazine/reserpine), or off-label program exists for intracranial hemorrhage; SLC18A2 is a monoamine vesicular transporter whose disease association is infantile parkinsonism-dystonia-2 with normal brain MRI and no hemorrhage/vascular phenotype (OMIM 618049), so the genetic score appears to be a spurious ontology roll-up with no clinical, preclinical, or class evidence.

No valbenazine or VMAT2-class trial in TBI/SCI/'injury'; only thin mechanistic literature exists, and it concerns INCREASED VMAT2 protecting dopamine neurons from neurotoxic (MPTP/methamphetamine) insult (PMC4489556) — the opposite direction to valbenazine's VMAT2 inhibition and not traumatic injury, so support is target-rationale only.
